look_here_first: Find the rhizomatous PERENNIAL base, then inspect the lower stem leaves: oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 6–12 mm wide, with truncate to slightly heart-shaped bases. At fruiting check the pappus, a tiny thickened ring or erose crown <0.1 mm, NOT the conspicuous ~25 bristles of C. ericoides.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Low, spreading or ascending perennial with rhizomes, not a distinct annual taproot; inspect the crown/rootstock.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, flat herbaceous leaves, proximal cauline blades oblong to lanceolate-oblong, typically 6–12 mm wide; bases truncate to subcordate; leaves diminish distally.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Small solitary terminal radiate heads with pale rays and yellow disk florets; flowering color overlaps congeners.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Pappus a minute thickened ring or erose crown under 0.1 mm (Flora of North America key).

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Examine basal and stem leaves including overlap and blade bases

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Examine mature cypsela pappus with magnification
